day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the Aerobus (€5.90 one-way) or the L9 Sud metro line (€5.15 with T-Casual card) to the city centre, then connect via metro or bus to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed evening stroll around the local neighbourhood to get your bearings. Grab a cold drink at a nearby terrace bar and unwind after the flight.

meals.breakfast: N/A – on the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Pick up a quick and affordable bite near the hotel – look for a local 'bocadillo' (filled baguette) or a menú del día at a neighbourhood bar for around €10–12. Alternatively, grab groceries from a nearby Mercadona or Lidl supermarket to keep costs low on arrival night.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) at the airport – it covers all metro, bus and tram journeys within Zone 1 and will save money throughout the trip. Sant Just Desvern is just outside Barcelona's city limits; the L3 metro (Zona Universitària stop) is your main gateway into the city centre.

day_by_day.morning: Head into Barcelona via metro to the Eixample district. Start the day with the **Sagrada Família Guided Tour** – book the basic entry + tower access in advance online (€26–33). Arrive early (opening is 09:00) to beat the summer crowds and the worst of the 28°C+ heat. The guided tour reveals Gaudí's intricate symbolism across the Nativity and Passion facades and the breathtaking interior forest of columns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short metro ride to **Passeig de Gràcia** – Barcelona's grand modernista boulevard. Stroll past the 'Block of Discord': Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller and Casa Lleó Morera. Admire the exteriors for free, then cool off in the shade of **Gràcia neighbourhood**. Explore the charming squares (Plaça del Sol, Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia) and browse independent boutiques. Rest at the hotel during the hottest part of the afternoon (14:00–17:00) if needed.
day_by_day.afternoon_activity_2: Late afternoon: Visit **Parc Güell** (€10 for the Monumental Zone, book online). Explore Gaudí's mosaic terraces and gingerbread gatehouses with sweeping views over the city. Go after 17:00 when it's slightly cooler.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Eixample or El Born area for Barcelona's famous nightlife warm-up. Start with 'vermut' (vermouth) hour around 19:00–21:00 at a local bar – a glass costs €2–4. Head to **El Born / Barceloneta** area for pre-drinks. Barcelona nightlife starts late; clubs don't fill up until midnight–01:00. Try free-entry bars along Carrer del Parlament (Sant Antoni neighbourhood) for a budget-friendly night out.

meals.breakfast: Café con leche and a croissant or tostada at a local café near the hotel or near Sagrada Família – budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Menú del día (set lunch menu) near Gràcia or Eixample – typically €11–14 for three courses including bread and a drink. Look for spots away from tourist hotspots.
meals.dinner: Pintxos or tapas crawl in El Born – order at the bar to keep costs down. Budget €12–15 for a satisfying spread of patatas bravas, croquetas and pan con tomate with a beer.

day_by_day.notes: August is peak season – book Sagrada Família tickets at least a week in advance online to avoid sell-outs and long queues. Wear light, breathable clothing and carry a water bottle; temperatures will hit ~29°C by midday.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to **Barceloneta** and walk along the seafront promenade (Passeig Marítim) in the cooler morning air. Explore the **Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic)** on foot – it's completely free. Wander through narrow medieval lanes, find the **Plaça Reial** (a beautiful neoclassical square with Gaudí-designed lampposts), the **Barcelona Cathedral** (free entry before 12:30 and after 17:30), and the Roman ruins of **Temple d'August** (free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the **Palau de la Música Catalana** – even if you're not attending a concert, the exterior is a stunning modernista gem by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Self-guided visits are available (€22), or simply admire the facade for free. Afterwards, explore **El Born market (Mercat de Santa Caterina)** – a colourful alternative to La Boqueria with fewer tourists and lower prices. Pick up fresh fruit, olives and local snacks. Spend the hottest hours (14:00–17:00) resting or in an air-conditioned café.
day_by_day.evening: **Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert** – attend a live performance at this UNESCO World Heritage modernista masterpiece. Tickets for smaller concerts can start from €18–35 depending on the programme; check the official website for August listings and book in advance. The stained-glass ceiling and ornate interior are jaw-dropping under concert lighting. Afterwards, join the nightlife in the **El Raval** neighbourhood – Carrer de Joaquín Costa has affordable bars with a local, artsy crowd.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastry (ensaïmada or croissant) and coffee at a bakery in the Gothic Quarter – €3–4.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh bocadillo or empanada from Mercat de Santa Caterina – budget €5–8 for a filling market lunch with fruit.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at a budget restaurant in El Born – try a set menú or a simple pasta/pizza spot. Budget €10–14. Alternatively, grab a quick falafel wrap in El Raval (€5–7) before the concert.

day_by_day.notes: The Palau de la Música Catalana concert schedule varies – check palaumusica.cat well in advance and book as soon as tickets open. Dress smart-casual for the concert. The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot; wear comfortable shoes as the cobblestones are uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to **Montjuïc** via the Paral·lel station and ride the free funicular (included with metro T-Casual card). Explore the **Fundació Joan Miró** (€14 entry – worth it for architecture and art lovers) or save money and walk the castle grounds of **Castell de Montjuïc** (€5, with panoramic views over the city and port). The hilltop is breezy and cooler than the city streets in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Montjuïc and head to **Poble Sec** neighbourhood for lunch. Afterwards, explore the **Pavillon Mies van der Rohe** (€5) – a minimalist architectural gem and a must for architecture enthusiasts. Then walk or metro to **Barceloneta beach** for a swim and a rest in the sea breeze. The beach is free; rent a sunbed for €5–8 or bring a towel.
day_by_day.evening: Barcelona's best budget nightlife evening. Start in **Sant Antoni** neighbourhood around 21:00 for vermouth and tapas. Then move to **Poble Sec** (Carrer de Blai – the famous pintxos street) for cheap eats and drinks. Later, head to **Barceloneta or Port Olímpic** for open-air beach bars (chiringuitos). Many clubs in the Port Olímpic area have free entry before 01:00 with a drink included. Dance until the early hours – this is peak Barcelona summer nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Tostada con tomate y aceite (toasted bread with tomato and olive oil) and café con leche at a local bar near the hotel – €3–5. A classic Catalan breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pintxos on Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec – most pintxos are €1–2 each; budget €8–12 for a satisfying lunch with a beer.
meals.dinner: Grab a fresh seafood 'bocadillo de calamares' or a grilled fish dish at a budget chiringuito on Barceloneta beach – budget €10–15. Or cook a simple meal back at the hotel to save money for drinks later.

day_by_day.notes: Montjuïc is very exposed to the sun – go early and bring sunscreen and water. The Carrer de Blai pintxos bars get very busy in the evening; lunchtime is quieter and equally good. Keep valuables secure in Barceloneta and the Gothic Quarter – pickpocketing is common in tourist areas.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – visit **La Barceloneta market** or the lesser-known **Mercat de l'Abaceria** in Gràcia for a local experience. Then take a final walk along **Passeig de Gràcia** to photograph the modernista architecture in the morning light before the crowds arrive. Pop into any free-entry church or courtyard you missed earlier in the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the **Bunkers del Carmel** – a free hilltop viewpoint in the Carmel neighbourhood offering arguably the best 360° panoramic view of Barcelona. It's a short hike or taxi ride from the metro (Alfons X station, L4). Bring water and snacks. This is a beloved local spot and completely free. Spend a couple of hours soaking in the view and taking photos. Return to the hotel to pack and check out.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on your departure schedule, enjoy a final farewell dinner in the city. If time allows, revisit a favourite neighbourhood for one last vermouth or cerveza on a terrace. Head to the airport via Aerobus or metro L9 Sud from Zona Universitària.

meals.breakfast: Café and croissant at a neighbourhood café – €3–5.
meals.lunch: Supermarket picnic or a final menú del día near the Bunkers area or Gràcia – €10–13.
meals.dinner: Budget farewell dinner – try a classic Catalan restaurant offering 'pa amb tomàquet' (bread with tomato), escalivada and grilled meat or fish. Look for a menú de noche or à la carte options under €15 per person in Gràcia or Eixample.

day_by_day.notes: The Bunkers del Carmel is especially magical at sunset – if your schedule allows, time your visit for around 19:30–20:30 for golden hour views. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours to reach the airport from Sant Just Desvern during peak summer traffic. The Aerobus departs from Plaça de Catalunya every 5–10 minutes and takes ~35 minutes to the airport.

day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit. Flight lands at El Prat Airport at 19:20. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Aerobus or L9 Sud metro line to connect toward Sant Just Desvern. Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Casual first-night stroll around Sant Just Desvern town center to get oriented. Grab a light dinner at a nearby local restaurant within walking distance of the hotel to decompress after travel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: La Bodegueta de Sant Just or a nearby neighbourhood tapas bar in Sant Just Desvern – budget €15–25 per person for wine, pa amb tomàquet, and tapas

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 evening very relaxed. The hotel is in Sant Just Desvern, roughly 15–20 minutes by car or bus from central Barcelona. Confirm your transport card (T-Casual 10-trip) at the airport to save money on metro and bus rides all week. August temperatures can still be warm at night (~22°C), so light clothing is fine.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Book the first entry slot (9:00 AM) to beat the August crowds and heat. The guided tour (~90 minutes) reveals Gaudí's intricate symbolism across the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like nave, and the towers. Pre-book tickets online well in advance as August slots sell out weeks ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, walk or take a short taxi to the Eixample district and explore the Modernista 'Block of Discord' on Passeig de Gràcia – admire Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside (enter Casa Batlló if budget allows, ~€35). Stroll La Pedrera (Casa Milà) exterior and rooftop if time permits. Rest at a shaded café during peak heat (2:00–4:00 PM).
day_by_day.evening: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk – Join a small-group or self-guided evening walking tour starting around 6:00 PM when temperatures drop. Wander the labyrinthine medieval streets, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and cross into El Born to see the Santa Maria del Mar basilica and the trendy boutique-lined streets. End the evening with drinks at a rooftop bar in El Born.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café near the hotel – croissant, coffee, fresh orange juice (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer Mallorca in Eixample – excellent mid-range tapas and montaditos, ~€20–28 per person
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born – classic Catalan tavern with cava and tapas, ~€20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks between 1:00–4:00 PM (avg high ~29°C). Plan outdoor walking for mornings and evenings. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestones in the Gothic Quarter. Carry a refillable water bottle – public drinking fountains are plentiful.

day_by_day.morning: Pavillon Mies van der Rohe & Montjuïc Architecture Trail – Head to Montjuïc by metro (Espanya station) + escalators or cable car. Start at the Barcelona Pavilion (opens 10:00 AM, ~€14) – a serene masterpiece of minimalist modern architecture with its iconic travertine, glass, and water. Continue along the Montjuïc architecture trail to the Palau Nacional (MNAC exterior), the Olympic Stadium, and the Calatrava telecommunications tower.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Montjuïc Castle for panoramic views over Barcelona and the port (cable car or walk up). Descend via the Jardins de Laribal for shade and greenery. Return to the hotel mid-afternoon for a rest during peak heat, or find a shaded terrace café near Plaça Espanya.
day_by_day.evening: Poble Sec & Montjuïc Nightlife Circuit – Begin with dinner at a pintxos bar on Carrer de Blai (the 'pintxos street' of Poble Sec) around 8:30 PM. Then head to Sala Apolo or Maumau Underground for live music or DJ sets. The area comes alive after 11:00 PM – enjoy Barcelona's legendary late-night culture.

meals.breakfast: Granja Viader-style café near the hotel or a bakery – pa amb tomàquet, coffee, fresh juice (~€6–10)
meals.lunch: Bar Calders in Poble Sec – relaxed neighbourhood bar with excellent Catalan lunch menu (menú del día ~€13–16 including wine)
meals.dinner: Carrer de Blai pintxos crawl – Bar Calders, Bodega Sepúlveda, or Quimet & Quimet (legendary standing tapas bar, cash only) – budget ~€18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Quimet & Quimet is tiny and cash-only – arrive early (7:00 PM) or expect a wait. The Montjuïc cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc) offers stunning views but can have queues in August – consider the funicular instead. Nightlife in Barcelona starts late; don't expect clubs to fill until midnight.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana Guided Morning Tour – Book a daytime guided tour (tours run from 9:00 AM, ~€22) of this breathtaking UNESCO World Heritage modernista concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. The stained-glass skylight, sculpted stage arch, and ornate ceramic details are extraordinary. Located in El Born / Sant Pere neighbourhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Palau, explore the nearby El Born Cultural Centre (free entry to the archaeological ruins of medieval Barcelona inside) and browse the boutiques and galleries of El Born. Head to Barceloneta beach in the early afternoon for a swim and to cool off – it's a 15-minute walk from El Born. Rent a sun lounger (~€6) and enjoy the Mediterranean.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert – Return for a live evening concert at the Palau (check schedule at palaumusica.cat – tickets typically €30–60 for mid-range seats). The hall is even more magical when lit up at night. Dress smart-casual. Arrive 30 minutes early to admire the foyer.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in El Raval or a café near the Palau – avocado toast, specialty coffee (~€8–12)
meals.lunch: La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta (cash only, closes early ~3 PM) – legendary local spot, birthplace of the bombas; or Bar Leo on Carrer Sant Carles – fresh seafood and rice dishes, ~€20–30 per person
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Bar del Pla in El Born – modern Catalan cuisine, ~€25–35 per person; or a lighter option at a nearby wine bar

day_by_day.notes: Book the evening concert tickets well in advance – August is peak season and popular concerts sell out. Check the Palau's website for the August programme. La Cova Fumada has no sign and no reservations – arrive when it opens. Barceloneta can be very crowded in August; go before 2:00 PM for a better spot.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell – Take the metro to Vallcarca or Lesseps and walk up to Park Güell (book timed entry tickets online, ~€10 for the Monumental Zone). Explore Gaudí's mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and the iconic dragon staircase with sweeping city views. Go early (8:00 AM opening) to avoid the worst of the crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Park Güell and head to Gràcia neighbourhood for a leisurely afternoon. Explore the charming Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, browse independent shops, and visit the Mercat de l'Abaceria (flea market). Return to the hotel in the late afternoon to pack and rest before a final evening out.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening farewell dinner in the city. Head to the Eixample or El Born for a proper sit-down Catalan dinner. Afterwards, take a final walk along La Rambla and the waterfront at Port Vell to soak in the Barcelona atmosphere. Return to the hotel by taxi or night bus.

meals.breakfast: Café Nou in Gràcia or a neighbourhood bakery near Park Güell – ensaïmada, coffee (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: La Pepita in Gràcia – creative montaditos and craft beer in a beautifully tiled space, ~€15–22 per person
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza or Bodega Sepúlveda for a relaxed mid-range farewell meal (~€25–35 per person with wine); or splurge slightly at Disfrutar's bar menu for a special last night (~€40–50)

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed entry is strictly enforced – do not miss your slot. August 47.5mm monthly rainfall means occasional afternoon thunderstorms are possible; carry a compact umbrella. For the return journey, confirm your departure transfer or taxi to El Prat Airport in advance – allow at least 45–60 minutes from Sant Just Desvern depending on traffic.

meals.dinner: Late dinner at Restaurante Àbac (1 Michelin star, ~20 min drive into Barcelona) or, for a more relaxed first night, dine at the hotel's own restaurant or a nearby upscale neighbourhood bistro such as Can Cortada in Horta – classic Catalan cuisine in a 14th-century farmhouse setting.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm your private airport transfer in advance. The hotel concierge can arrange a late dinner reservation on arrival day.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel, then a private car transfer (~30 min) to the Eixample district for the Sagrada Família Guided Tour. Book a premium skip-the-line guided tour (ideally with tower access) to explore Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica in depth – discover the intricate symbolism of the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like nave, and the breathtaking stained-glass light show. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, walk or take a short taxi to Passeig de Gràcia for a self-guided architecture stroll along the 'Block of Discord' – admire Casa Batlló (consider the premium 'Magic Nights' evening ticket for later in the trip), Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera. Enjoy a long, leisurely lunch at Lasarte (2 Michelin stars, on Carrer de Mallorca) – one of Barcelona's finest dining rooms. Spend the afternoon exploring the Eixample grid at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon_note: Optional: book a private guided tour of Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) in the afternoon for an immersive architectural deep-dive.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Palau de la Música Catalana for an Evening Concert – a live performance inside this UNESCO World Heritage modernista masterpiece by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. The stained-glass skylight and ornate interior make this an unmissable sensory experience. Dress smart-casual or smart.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Sercotel Porta Barcelona or stop at a premium café such as Federal Café or Faborit on arrival in Eixample.
meals.lunch: Lasarte Restaurant (Carrer de Mallorca, 259) – contemporary Basque-Catalan haute cuisine; reserve well in advance.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at El Nacional Barcelona (Passeig de Gràcia) – a grand food hall with four distinct restaurants under one spectacular roof, ideal for a relaxed pre-show meal.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tower access and Palau de la Música concert tickets well in advance – both sell out quickly in August. Private transfer recommended between hotel and city centre.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, take a private transfer to the Gothic Quarter for the Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk. Join a small-group premium guided tour (or hire a private architectural guide) through Barcelona's medieval labyrinth – the Roman walls, Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and the Pont del Bisbe bridge. Cross into El Born to admire the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar and the stunning iron-and-glass Mercat de Santa Caterina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon in El Born – browse the boutiques and galleries, then visit the El Born Cultural Centre (built over the ruins of the 1714 neighbourhood). Enjoy a long lunch at Espai Mescladís or the acclaimed El Xampanyet cava bar for a more casual but authentic experience, or upgrade to a table at Koy Shunka (Japanese-Catalan fusion, near the Gothic Quarter) for a premium afternoon meal.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a rest and to change. In the evening, experience the Poble Sec & Montjuïc Nightlife Circuit – begin with creative pintxos and natural wines at a top Carrer de Blai bar, then move to a rooftop cocktail bar on Montjuïc (such as La Caseta del Migdia for open-air sunset drinks), before heading to a premium club or live music venue such as Sala Apolo or Paral·lel theatre district for late-night entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a stop at Bar del Pla in El Born – a beloved neighbourhood institution.
meals.lunch: Koy Shunka (Carrer dels Copons, 7) – refined Japanese-Catalan omakase; reserve ahead.
meals.dinner: Pintxos and small plates along Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec, followed by cocktails at a Montjuïc rooftop bar. Budget for premium drinks at the nightlife venues.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for the Gothic Quarter walk – cobblestones are uneven. The nightlife circuit runs late; plan to return to the hotel by private taxi after midnight. August nights are warm (~22°C), so light evening attire is fine.

day_by_day.morning: A slower morning after the late night – enjoy a relaxed hotel breakfast, then take a private transfer to Montjuïc for the Pavillon Mies van der Rohe & Montjuïc Architecture Trail. Begin at the iconic Barcelona Pavilion, a seminal work of modernist architecture built for the 1929 World Exhibition – its travertine, marble, and glass planes remain revolutionary. Continue along the Montjuïc trail to the Palau Nacional (MNAC), the Fundació Joan Miró, and the Olympic Ring for a panoramic view of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Montjuïc via cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc) for spectacular views over the port and city. Head to Barceloneta or the Port Olímpic waterfront for a premium seafood lunch. Spend the afternoon at leisure – consider a private yacht charter for 2–3 hours along the Barcelona coastline (bookable through the hotel concierge), or relax at a luxury beach club such as W Barcelona's Eclipse or Carpe Diem Beach Club (CDLC).
day_by_day.evening: Dress up for a special evening: cocktails at the rooftop bar of the W Barcelona hotel (Eclipse Bar, 26th floor) with sweeping Mediterranean views, followed by a tasting-menu dinner at Disfrutar (ranked among the World's 50 Best Restaurants) – a theatrical, avant-garde experience by former elBulli chefs. Book months in advance.

meals.lunch: La Mar Salada (Passeig de Joan de Borbó) – refined Catalan seafood with sea views, or a premium beach club lunch at CDLC.
meals.dinner: Disfrutar (Carrer de Villarroel, 163) – avant-garde tasting menu; one of the world's best restaurants. Reserve as early as possible.

day_by_day.notes: The Barcelona Pavilion opens at 10:00; arriving early avoids the midday heat. The Telefèric de Montjuïc cable car may have queues in August – a private guide can help manage timing. Disfrutar requires reservations months ahead for August dates.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – enjoy a leisurely checkout breakfast at the hotel. If time allows before departure, take a short drive to the Collserola hills above the city for a morning walk with panoramic views, or revisit a favourite neighbourhood café in Eixample or El Born for a final cortado and croissant. Visit any last-minute design or architecture shops along Passeig de Gràcia (Vinçon, BD Barcelona Design) for premium souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final long lunch at Cinc Sentits (5 Senses) – an intimate, Michelin-starred restaurant celebrating Catalan produce with a refined tasting menu. Alternatively, for a more casual farewell, try Bar Calders in Sant Antoni for vermouth and tapas in a lively local atmosphere. Arrange a private transfer back to El Prat Airport with ample time.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast – savour it as a final luxury moment.
meals.lunch: Cinc Sentits (Carrer d'Entença, 60) – Michelin-starred Catalan tasting menu; a perfect farewell meal.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the airport (El Prat has premium lounges including the TAP Portugal VIP lounge).

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for the airport transfer and check-in. Consider purchasing a bottle of Catalan cava or a design piece from BD Barcelona as a luxury memento of the trip.
